Streets, schools and getting around Deep Cove

items.t: Deep Cove is a waterfront village in the District of North Vancouver at the municipality's far eastern edge, on Indian Arm at the foot of Mount Seymour — the handful of streets around Gallant Avenue, Deep Cove Road and Panorama Drive. Deep Cove is confirmed in the District's Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900, as one of six Village Centres (with Lions Gate, Queensdale, Maplewood, Parkgate and Edgemont). Exact official boundary streets for the village are not verified — no OCP schedule or District page read states them.

Condo stock actually concentrates on the village's two core streets: Gallant Avenue, the village's main street (the retail row and two of the three apartment addresses), and Panorama Drive, the waterfront loop around Panorama Park. The surrounding plateau streets are detached houses under the District's R1 and R2 zones.

There is effectively one road in and out: Deep Cove Road / Gallant Avenue into the village, with Dollarton Highway west to Mount Seymour Parkway, Phibbs Exchange and Highway 1. TransLink buses reach the village from Phibbs Exchange via Dollarton Highway and Mount Seymour Parkway, terminating at Panorama Drive / Gallant Avenue in the village, and since September 7, 2026 the R2 RapidBus extension via Phibbs Exchange gives the village's bus corridor a one-seat ride to Metrotown.

Anchors: Panorama Park on Panorama Drive (beach, swimming area, picnic shelter, launch for kayaks and small boats, Deep Cove Yacht Club and the Indian Arm view); Seycove Secondary, 1204 Caledonia Avenue; Cove Cliff Elementary, 1818 Banbury Road; Deep Cove Park, 1991 Rockcliff Road. The nearest SkyTrain station is none within the District — the SkyTrain connection is by bus to downtown Vancouver over the Second Narrows, or by bus to Phibbs and the R2.
Nearby areas: Parkgate (west, under Mount Seymour Parkway), Woodlands and Indian River (north along Indian Arm), and Dollarton / Windsor Park (south-west along Dollarton Highway).

blocks.text: Good to know about Deep Cove

items.t: The secondary school's name is an Indigenous place name, gifted in 2022. Seycove Secondary's gifted name, sə́yəmətən, was shared by the səlilwətaɬ (Tsleil-Waututh) Nation in June 2022 — "place of serenity near the water" — and the village sits on the Nation's inlet territory.

The District endorsed the Deep Cove Parking and Access Implementation Plan in 2015, and its April 22, 2024 Parking Review presentation to Council covered pay parking, resident parking and time-limited parking — the scarcity a summer visitor sees at Panorama Park is structural, not seasonal bad luck.

The Quarry Rock trailhead is inside the village. The Baden Powell Trail and the Quarry Rock hike are accessed from Panorama Park, and Deep Cove Park at 1991 Rockcliff Road adds a tennis court, playground and gravel field — the trail traffic shares the same streets and parking as the two Gallant Avenue buildings.

One of the village's two named stratas is part commercial. Deep Cove Estates' ground floor is strata retail and office space zoned VC-G on Gallant Avenue — the strata's insurance, parking and common-area decisions are made with commercial owners at the table, which a buyer reading only the residential listings would not see.
The village's growth is capped by its own OCP designation.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Deep Cove
Streets, schools and getting around Deep Cove

items.t: Deep Cove is the waterfront village at the District of North Vancouver's far eastern edge, on the shore of Indian Arm at the foot of Mount Seymour, built around Gallant Avenue, Deep Cove Road and Panorama Drive. Deep Cove is one of the six Village Centres named in the District's Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900 (with Lions Gate, Queensdale, Maplewood, Parkgate and Edgemont) — a confirmed District planning name. Exact boundary streets: Not verified; the confirmed anchors are the village core on lower Gallant Avenue, Panorama Park on Panorama Drive, and the Cove Cliff / Banbury Road streets above the village.

Neighbours: Cove Cliff and Dollarton to the west along Dollarton Highway, Parkgate and Seymour to the south-west at Mount Seymour Parkway, Woodlands and Indian Arm to the north up the inlet, and Belcarra across Indian Arm. Deep Cove Road / Gallant Avenue and Dollarton Highway are the only road in and out — west to Mount Seymour Parkway, Phibbs Exchange and Highway 1; there is no second road connection north up Indian Arm for cars.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: at most one small pocket — the Caledonia Avenue / Panorama Drive corner above the village, where the Cove Gardens townhouse listing in sits. Everything else verified in the village is detached houses and three small apartment buildings.

Transit: local buses connect the village terminus on Panorama Drive / Gallant Avenue to Phibbs Exchange via Dollarton Highway and Mount Seymour Parkway; there is no SkyTrain station or SeaBus terminal in or near Deep Cove, and Phibbs Exchange is the rapid-transit connection point. Since September 7, 2026 the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus runs one-seat from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown, every 6–7 minutes at peak.

Schools: SD44 catchments are address-based, elementary (K–7) and secondary (8–12) only, with no middle tier. Cove Cliff Elementary, 1818 Banbury Road, is the elementary school in Deep Cove itself, and Seycove Secondary Community School, 1204 Caledonia Avenue — gifted the Indigenous place-based name sə́yəmətən ("place of good water") by the Tsleil-Waututh Nation in June 2022 — is the secondary school beside the village; Seycove's family of schools also includes Dorothy Lynas and Sherwood Park elementaries, so a street west of the village may feed a Parkgate-side school. The address-level catchment result for Deep Cove homes is not verified from the SD44 material read — check each address with SD44.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Deep Cove

items.t: Form B diligence (strata purchases generally; the document that would settle Cove Gardens): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For Cove Gardens, the first diligence step is confirming strata title itself — title and strata plan, not a directory line.

District zoning: District of North Vancouver Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525 — the R1 zone minimum lot is 4,000 m² with 30 m width and 34 m depth, and the R2 zone minimum lot is 660 m² with 18 m width and 34 m depth, with modifiers R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m; an R2 principal building may include a secondary suite, and a coach house is a dwelling unit accessory to and detached from the principal dwelling unit.

Hazards and permits: OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets seven Development Permit Areas, including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — Deep Cove's forested slope, creek and shoreline lots can fall in several at once, and the District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports, including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m.

District property taxes and utilities: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value. District single-family utility fees in 2026 include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60, with combined single-family utilities of $2,571.20.

blocks.text: Good to know about Deep Cove

items.t: The village's one townhouse name hides behind two addresses and an uncited directory.

The secondary school carries a gifted Indigenous name. Seycove Secondary was gifted the place-based name sə́yəmətən ("place of good water") by the Tsleil-Waututh Nation in June 2022 — the name a buyer will see on District material for the school beside the village.
The village core is mid-redesign.

Panorama Park is the trailhead, not just the view. The park on Panorama Drive — beach access, open green space, picnic shelter and the Deep Cove Yacht Club / Indian Arm view — is the eastern access point for the Baden Powell Trail, and the Quarry Rock lookout is reached on that trail from Panorama Drive. Deep Cove Park, 1991 Rockcliff Road, is the second District park north of the village core.
Mount Seymour Provincial Park is the backdrop and the ski hill.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Deep Cove
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established village and waterfront lots: detached houses under the District's R1 and R2 detached residential zones in Section 525 of Zoning Bylaw 3210, on the village, Cove Cliff and waterfront streets above Indian Arm, with the village-centre mixed-use form on the Gallant Avenue core under the OCP Village Centre designation; predominantly freehold detached, including waterfront freehold on the inlet streets. The village street pattern is historic subdivision fabric — built lots, not a lot offering.

Lot character, as the bylaw states it: R1 minimum lot 4,000 m² with 30 m width and 34 m depth; R2 minimum lot 660 m² with 18 m width and 34 m depth; modifiers R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m. Zone minimums only — not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone on a single lot is confirmed through the District's GeoWeb.

Serviced position, as the District states it: District single-family utility fees in 2026 include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60, with combined single-family utilities of $2,571.20 — the village's established lots sit inside that District system on the District's wording. Parcel-level servicing beyond that wording: Not verified; confirm the specific parcel with the District.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Deep Cove is documented; parcel-level ALR status is listed not verified there. No ALR percentage split is stated — check any specific parcel on Agricultural Land Commission mapping.

Foreshore position — the village's distinctive land diligence: for waterfront and moorage-adjacent parcels, foreshore, dock and lease status is confirmed parcel by parcel — no Deep Cove foreshore tenure fact is confirmed, so any moorage claim is not verified until the title and District records say otherwise. The District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports, including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m.

blocks.text: Assemblies, development sites and proposals

items.t: No approved major residential project or presale specific to Deep Cove village is confirmed on a District source: — not verified. The Livable Deep Cove project (lower Gallant Avenue pedestrian area) is documented as village-core implementation work under the OCP, not a housing project: in the District's September 2022 engagement results, 818 online surveys were completed and 82% of respondents strongly or somewhat strongly supported change on lower Gallant. It creates no lots and is never inventory.

: the District endorsed a Deep Cove Parking and Access Implementation Plan in 2015 and returned with a Parking Review implementation plan presentation to Council on April 22, 2024, covering on-street pay parking, resident parking and time-limited parking in the village — priced context for village-core lots, not supply.

items.t: Nearby areas: Cove Cliff and Dollarton (west, along Dollarton Highway), Parkgate and Seymour (south-west, at Mount Seymour Parkway), Woodlands and Indian Arm (north, up the inlet), and Belcarra across Indian Arm.

Roads and access: Deep Cove Road / Gallant Avenue and Dollarton Highway are the only road in and out — west to Mount Seymour Parkway, Phibbs Exchange and Highway 1; there is no second road connection north up Indian Arm for cars. Transit: local buses run from Phibbs Exchange via Dollarton Highway and Mount Seymour Parkway to the village terminus on Panorama Drive / Gallant Avenue; since September 7, 2026 the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus runs one-seat from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown, roughly 5 a.m.–2 a.m., every 6–7 minutes at peak.

Village anchors: Panorama Park, on Panorama Drive directly in front of Deep Cove, is a compact waterfront park with a view of the Deep Cove Yacht Club and Indian Arm, beach access, a picnic shelter and a short walk to the playground, and is the eastern access point for the Baden Powell Trail (Quarry Rock lookout above the village); Deep Cove Park is at 1991 Rockcliff Road, north of the village core. Mount Seymour Provincial Park rises directly behind the Seymour/Deep Cove side. Nearest hospital: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Deep Cove

items.t: : if a Deep Cove lot's title confirms bare-land strata tenure (the Cove Gardens question is exactly this, held not confirmed in townhomes), the lot is strata tenure in full: Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Deep Cove ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within the principal residence only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of the land's value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about Deep Cove

items.t: The secondary school carries a gifted name (June 2022): Seycove Secondary was gifted the Indigenous place-based name sə́yəmətən ("place of good water") by the Tsleil-Waututh Nation — the village sits on Tsleil-Waututh territory at the head of Indian Arm, context a waterfront buyer should know before foreshore or dock work.

The village voted for its own pedestrian core (September 2022): 818 online surveys were completed in the District's Livable Deep Cove engagement and 82% of respondents strongly or somewhat strongly supported change on lower Gallant Avenue — the Gallant core a lot buyer sees today is mid-implementation, not finished form.

The R2 extension changed the transit math (September 7, 2026): the R2 RapidBus now runs one-seat from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown every 6–7 minutes at peak — the fastest transit leg a Deep Cove rider reaches, and the frequent-transit proximity that feeds the District's SSMUH classification for lots near the connection.

faq.a: Three small apartment buildings, all 1980s–1990: Panorama Place (2181 Panorama Drive, 11 units), Deep Cove Estates (4390 Gallant Avenue, 21 units), and an apartment building at 4323 Gallant Avenue whose name is not confirmed on a citable source.
faq.q: How much condo stock does Deep Cove actually have?

faq.a: Yes, long-term — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind.
faq.q: Deep Cove Estates' directory says rentals are not allowed. Can I rent my unit out?

faq.a: Only a 55-or-older bylaw is valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, and the directory does not state the age or the bylaw terms — that is not confirmed until the filed bylaws are read on the Form B. Exemptions cover legacy residents, live-in caregivers and, from May 1, 2023, younger spouses/partners and defined children.
faq.q: Panorama Place is listed with "age restrictions." What does that mean for a younger buyer?

faq.a: From the published sources: Panorama Place allows pets with restrictions, and Deep Cove Estates allows pets. Confirm the exact bylaw wording on the Form B — pet bylaws still bind.
faq.q: Are pets allowed in the village buildings?

faq.a: No — it is a mixed-use strata on Gallant Avenue: commercial listings for its ground-floor units describe strata retail and office units zoned VC-G (Village Commercial – Gallant Avenue). A residential buyer is sharing a strata with commercial owners on the village's main street.
faq.q: Is Deep Cove Estates purely residential?

faq.a: Everything else verified in the village is detached houses and three small apartment buildings.
faq.q: Are there any townhomes in Deep Cove at all?

faq.a: That is the complex's core diligence item: pull title and, if strata, the Form B and strata plan before pricing it as either tenure — do not rely on a directory line.
faq.q: Is Cove Gardens strata or fee-simple?

faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, even though the building directory still prints "rentals not allowed" for Deep Cove Estates. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.
faq.q: Can I rent out a unit in Deep Cove Estates?

faq.a: The waterfront village at the District of North Vancouver's eastern edge on Indian Arm — Panorama Park and Deep Cove Park on the water, the Gallant Avenue village core (one of the District OCP's six Village Centres), and the Baden Powell Trail / Quarry Rock trailhead at Panorama Park.
faq.q: What is Deep Cove known for?

faq.a: Cove Cliff Elementary, 1818 Banbury Road (K–7), in the village area, and Seycove Secondary Community School, 1204 Caledonia Avenue (8–12), beside the village; catchments are address-based, so confirm the exact address with SD44.
